title: LeBron Passed on a Reported $15M for a Pizza Stake

beats.say: In 2015, LeBron James walked away from a reported fifteen million dollars to back a pizza chain.
beats.visual: a lone basketball under a single hard sodium light on an empty court at dawn, a paper takeout bag with a red logo-free pizza box beside it, long shadows

beats.say: McDonald's had paid him about four million dollars a year.
beats.visual: close on a stack of crisp cash held by a rubber band on a steel counter, cold fluorescent light, shallow depth of field

beats.say: Another four years meant roughly fifteen million, his business partner says.
beats.visual: a thick paper contract and a pen on a dark conference table, one desk lamp, a glass wall with city lights behind it

beats.say: So he backed a small pizza chain instead, with about a million dollars of his own.
beats.visual: an open pizza oven glowing orange in a narrow restaurant kitchen at night, flour dust in the air, a chef's silhouette

beats.say: A flat fee ends when the contract ends. A stake keeps growing with the company.
beats.visual: two doors side by side in a long concrete corridor, the left one shut and dim, the right one open with warm light spilling out

beats.say: ESPN reported he owns more than ten percent of Blaze. So what was that stake worth?
beats.visual: a pie chart-like pizza cut into slices on a dark table, one slice lifted away trailing steam, moody overhead light

beats.say: By 2022, Forbes estimated it at about thirty million dollars, roughly thirty times his first investment, on paper.
beats.visual: a tall glass tower at blue hour, a single window lit gold at the top floor, wet street reflections below

beats.say: In 2008 he took a small stake in Beats for promoting the headphones. Was that a fluke?
beats.visual: a pair of over-ear headphones resting on a black speaker in a dark studio, red light strip, dust motes

beats.say: Apple bought Beats for three billion dollars in 2014, and he reportedly collected about thirty million.
beats.visual: a heavy bank vault door half open in dark shadow, one beam of light across brushed steel

beats.say: So why choose a stake over guaranteed money? A check pays once. Ownership keeps paying as the company grows.
beats.visual: a single oak tree growing through cracked concrete in an empty lot at sunrise, long golden light

beats.say: The catch: he was already among the league's highest-paid players, and most equity deals pay nothing.
beats.visual: an empty arena tunnel with one lit exit at the end, wet floor, harsh overhead lights, no people

beats.say: Check or stake? Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: a lone figure in silhouette on a rooftop at dusk looking at a city skyline, a gold light on the horizon

caption:
A fixed check ends with the contract. A stake keeps growing. 🍕

#money #personalfinance #wealth #equity #business
description: In 2015 LeBron James let his McDonald's endorsement lapse, a reported $14-15 million over four years, and backed Blaze Pizza instead. Forbes later estimated his stake at about $30 million. The lesson: ask what you can own, not only what you will be paid. Figures are reported or estimated; he was already among the highest-paid players alive.
first_comment: Guaranteed $15 million, or about $1 million into a company you believe in. Which one do you take?

facts.claim: In 2015 LeBron James did not renew his McDonald's endorsement; his business partner Maverick Carter said that meant walking away from about $14-15 million over four years.
McDonald's extended the deal in 2012 for roughly $4 million a year.
He was an early Blaze Pizza investor in 2012 with a first investment of about $1 million (ESPN said less than $1 million).
facts.basis: PitchBook 2018; ESPN as cited by Investopedia.

facts.claim: ESPN's Darren Rovell reported he owns more than 10% of Blaze Pizza.
Forbes estimated his Blaze stake at about $30 million in 2022. This is an estimate, not a sale.
In 2008 he received a small Beats stake in exchange for promoting the headphones; Apple bought Beats for $3 billion in 2014 and he reportedly received about $30 million in cash and stock.
He was among the highest-paid NBA players when he made these choices (Forbes ranked him No. 1 for 2022-23, $124.5 million).

loop_map.stakes: LeBron James choosing between a reported $15 million of McDonald's money and a stake in a small pizza chain in 2015.
loop_map.big_question: Why did LeBron James turn down guaranteed money for a small pizza chain?
loop_map.assume: A guaranteed check is the safe choice.
loop_map.reveal: Ownership kept paying: Forbes estimates the stake at about $30 million, and an earlier Beats stake paid a reported $30 million.
